background_story: Joaquin was a 5th-century monk who lived in the deserts of Egypt. He was deeply devoted to the teachings of Cyril of Alexandria and became a fervent advocate for the doctrine of monophysitism, which posited that Jesus Christ had only one, divine nature. Joaquin's conviction in this doctrine led him to engage in heated debates with his fellow monks, who adhered to the Chalcedonian view of Jesus' dual nature. Despite the controversy, Joaquin's passion and erudition earned him the respect of his peers. He spent years studying the scriptures and the writings of the early Church Fathers, seeking to deepen his understanding of the mystery of Christ's nature. Joaquin's unwavering commitment to monophysitism ultimately led him to become a leader among the Egyptian monks, who saw him as a champion of orthodoxy.
